mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes G Class G 500 engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Mercedes G Class G 500 engine replacement typically costs between £4,200 and £6,800 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. M113 V8 units range from £4,200 to £6,800 supply only. M112 V6 units (G 320) range from £3,800 to £6,000. Rebuilt M113 (G 500): £4,200-£6,800 supply only. Rebuilt M112 (G 320): £3,800-£6,000 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £1,200-£3,500 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the M113 V8 engine in the G 500 reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M113 is regarded as one of Mercedes' greatest achievements - durable, simple in design, and delivering impressive longevity when properly maintained. However, age brings some well-documented issues. Oil leaks from valve cover gaskets and breather covers are common. Timing chain tensioner wear causes cold-start rattle. Harmonic balancer failure can occur on higher-mileage examples. With preventative maintenance, 200,000+ miles is realistic.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M113 timing chain tensioner wear in a G 500?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M113's hydraulic timing chain tensioner typically shows warning signs before complete failure - a rattling noise on cold start is the most common symptom. Rattling or clanking noise from the front of the engine on cold startup. Noise that lasts more than 2 seconds indicates significant chain slack. Rattle that disappears within 1 second may be normal hydraulic bleed-down. If ignored, the chain can skip teeth and cause catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my G 320 or G 500 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., valve cover gaskets, timing chain tensioner, harmonic balancer). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or multiple major failures. Valve cover gasket replacement at specialist: £300-£500 - excellent value. Timing chain tensioner replacement: £250-£400 - do this at first sign of rattle. Full M113 rebuild: £4,200-£6,800 - for catastrophic failure or 200k+ miles. Given G 500 values (£12,000-£30,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my G 320 or G 500 has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix (e.g., M112, M113). V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block (visible from under vehicle). G 320 (1998-2005): M112.945 (3.2L V6). G 500 (1998-2008): M113.962 (5.0L V8). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used G 320 or G 500 engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a G Class petrol. The complex 4MATIC system, gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. 4MATIC transfer case alignment requires specialist knowledge. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation needed. Engine and gearbox must be separated correctly. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz G Class G 350 / G 500 (Older Petrol) Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz G Class G 320 and G 500 rely on the M112 V6 and M113 V8 engine families - both considered among Mercedes' most reliable petrol engines. However, age and mileage bring well-documented issues: oil leaks from valve cover gaskets, timing chain tensioner wear on higher-mileage examples, and harmonic balancer failures. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common G Class petrol engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M112 / M113 Oil Leaks - Why G Class Petrol Engines Drip Oil
problems.rootCause: The valve cover gaskets and breather cover seals harden and crack due to repeated hot/cold engine cycles, allowing oil to weep onto the exhaust manifolds. This is a common problem on both M112 and M113 engines as they age.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Valve Cover Gasket Replacement (Both Sides)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gaskets, breather cover seals, new gaskets and RTV sealant
Replace valve cover gaskets, breather covers, PCV system, oil filter housing gasket
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles; recommended if multiple leaks present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M112 or M113 with new gaskets, seals, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic failure or 200k+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical G 320 is worth £8,000-£18,000 depending on condition, while a G 500 is worth £12,000-£30,000【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. For the G 500, the full replacement cost of £4,200-£6,800 is modest relative to vehicle value. For a G 320, evaluate repair vs replacement based on overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Oil leaks on M112 and M113 engines are rarely urgent but should not be ignored. The specialist valve cover gasket replacement at £300-£500 is excellent value and should last 80k+ miles. If you're already addressing one leak, consider doing the full top-end reseal - the labour overlaps significantly and the additional parts cost is modest.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M112 or M113 Mercedes Benz G Class petrol engine prices

problems.h4: M113 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the G 500 Rattles on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The hydraulic timing chain tensioner can lose oil pressure retention when parked, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. If left unaddressed, the chain can skip teeth with catastrophic valve-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace hydraulic tensioner only, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-40k miles; only viable if no chain damage yet

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace both chains, all tensioners, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles; corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M113 with new chain, tensioner and upgraded guides
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; required if chain has jumped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a G 500 worth £12,000-£30,000, the tensioner-only specialist fix at £250-£400 is excellent value. The full chain set at £1,400-£2,200 is also justified given the vehicle's value. Only consider full engine replacement for catastrophic failure or 200k+ mile examples.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of cold-start rattle, do the tensioner-only specialist fix (£250-£400). If the rattle lasts more than 2 seconds or you've ignored it for 10k+ miles, go straight to the full chain set. The M113's SOHC design means chain failure is catastrophic - preventative attention is far cheaper than engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M113 Mercedes Benz G Class G 500 engine prices

problems.h4: M112 / M113 Harmonic Balancer Failure - Why G Class Petrol Engines Lose Power Steering
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz G Class G 320 (M112.945) and G 500 (M113.962, 1998-2008)
problems.rootCause: The crankshaft pulley/harmonic balancer can fail, separating the outer ring from the inner hub. This can cause loss of power steering assist, belt drive failure, and in some cases, damage to surrounding components.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace crankshaft pulley/harmonic balancer, inspect belt and tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative or at first sign of wobble/rumble

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M112 or M113 with new balancer, belts, and tensioners
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty; for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On either a G 320 or G 500, the harmonic balancer replacement at £350-£550 is a sensible preventative repair. Ignoring it risks belt failure and potential engine damage.
problems.recommendation: The harmonic balancer is a known weak point on M112 and M113 engines. If you notice any wobble, rumble, or belt noise from the front of the engine, replace the balancer immediately. It's a straightforward job for a specialist and far cheaper than the collateral damage of a complete failure.
